views.observation: Recognizable Keelmaw cues, but huge regular gold spikes dominate a low flat barrel. Long narrow squared jaw and round protruding eye weaken expression.
Whole stance clear, but giant spines and a raised thick tail compete with the narrow straight-front mouth. No convincing brow; central keel is a plain bar.
Four-foot stance holds. Large angular tail segments and uniformly spaced spines read as a mechanical assembly more than a faceted reptile.
Long crocodile profile is readable; three tall parallel dorsal rows and flat body line are too regular. Jaw is a rectangular tooth grille.
Coherent tail curl and visible amber eye. Torso is a long plain band with very large triangular spikes; forelimbs and hindlimbs have scant scute breakup.
Full 3D anatomy. Three near-straight gold rails dominate the back, and sharp tail kinks expose construction; rectangular head and strap ends remain highly regular.
Body and feet complete, but long straight head and three tall spike files overwhelm the face. Mouth is a thin central-divider opening.
Back reads as a rectangular gridded spiked saddle; broad segmented tail is noticeably kinked. Rope and barnacles remain present.
Toothed maw, barnacles and gold spines make identity recognizable. Low flat torso, exposed button eye and polygonal hook tail diverge substantially from concept.
Consistent look across orbit, no billboard. Overlarge gold wedges and long flat torso outweigh modest plating; mouth and eye stay too schematic.
